# Anvil

> Opinionated .NET & Akka.NET conventions - forged from real projects.

This file is a machine-readable index of all conventions on [https://anvil.st0o0.net](https://anvil.st0o0.net).
For the complete content in a single file, see [llms-full.txt](https://anvil.st0o0.net/llms-full.txt).

## Getting Started

- [Project Scaffolding](https://anvil.st0o0.net/getting-started/project-scaffolding/): Every new project starts from one of the template repositories. They include the root-level files, CI workflows, and tooling described below - so you get a working setup without manual assembly.
- [Solution Structure](https://anvil.st0o0.net/getting-started/solution-structure/): A multi-project solution with strict domain isolation. Structure is enforced by architecture tests, not by convention alone.
- [Dev Environment](https://anvil.st0o0.net/getting-started/dev-environment/): The application runs in Docker during development, together with the services it depends on. This keeps local behavior close to production.

## C# Conventions

- [C# Coding Standards](https://anvil.st0o0.net/csharp/coding-standards/): Formatting and style rules enforced by tooling. If a rule is not machine-checked, it is still expected in review.
- [Type Design](https://anvil.st0o0.net/csharp/type-design/): Choose the type kind by what the type is for. The defaults below keep types small, safe to share, and cheap to reason about.
- [Enum Conventions](https://anvil.st0o0.net/csharp/enum-conventions/): These rules are violated often and are costly to fix once values are stored or on the wire. Follow them exactly.
- [Async Patterns](https://anvil.st0o0.net/csharp/async-patterns/): Rules for asynchronous code, cancellation, time, and concurrency.

## Akka.NET

- [Actor Design Conventions](https://anvil.st0o0.net/akka/actor-design/): Actors are **thin plumbing**: message routing, persistence hooks and lifecycle. Domain logic and mutable domain state live elsewhere (see [State Management](state-management)).
- [Actor State Pattern](https://anvil.st0o0.net/akka/state-management/): The "Pathfinder pattern": all mutable domain state lives in a dedicated state class. The actor only routes messages and calls `Apply`.
- [Message Conventions](https://anvil.st0o0.net/akka/messaging/): Command and its responses live in one file.
- [Persistence Conventions](https://anvil.st0o0.net/akka/persistence/): Three tools, each with exactly one job.
- [Akka.Streams Discipline](https://anvil.st0o0.net/akka/streams/): These rules are the ones broken and corrected most often. Read them before writing any stream.
- [Cluster & Sharding](https://anvil.st0o0.net/akka/cluster/): Three hosting shapes, each with a fixed naming convention.
- [Supervision Strategies](https://anvil.st0o0.net/akka/supervision/): Supervision decides what happens when a child actor throws. Defaults are good; deviate deliberately.

## API Design

- [Minimal API Endpoint Conventions](https://anvil.st0o0.net/api/minimal-api/): Endpoints are thin transport adapters. They translate HTTP into a message, ask a domain actor, and translate the response back into an `IResult`.
- [API Models & Mapping](https://anvil.st0o0.net/api/models-and-mapping/): API models are a separate type world from domain messages. Mapping extensions are the explicit bridge between the two.

## Testing

- [Testing Philosophy](https://anvil.st0o0.net/testing/philosophy/): Tests exist to pin down behavior and catch regressions. They do not exist to
- [Assertion Conventions](https://anvil.st0o0.net/testing/assertions/): Patterns for xUnit assertions. The goal is failures that point at the cause and
- [Actor Testing](https://anvil.st0o0.net/testing/actor-testing/): Conventions for testing Akka.NET actors. Examples assume xUnit.
- [Mutation Testing with Stryker.NET](https://anvil.st0o0.net/testing/mutation-testing/): Mutation testing changes production code in small ways (`>` to `>=`, `+` to `-`,
- [Architecture Tests with ArchUnitNET](https://anvil.st0o0.net/testing/architecture-tests/): Architecture tests turn structural conventions into failing builds. They live in

## DI & Configuration

- [DI Conventions](https://anvil.st0o0.net/config/dependency-injection/): Dependency injection is organized per domain and composed in `Program.cs`. The container is never queried by application code.
- [Options Pattern](https://anvil.st0o0.net/config/options-pattern/): Do not build custom singleton resolution when `IOptions<T>` plus `PostConfigure` already exists. Reaching for a bespoke resolver, plan object, or info service is the most common mistake in this area.

## Observability

- [Metrics Conventions](https://anvil.st0o0.net/observability/metrics/): Metrics use `System.Diagnostics.Metrics` with one meter per domain, exported through OpenTelemetry to Prometheus.
- [Logging Conventions](https://anvil.st0o0.net/observability/logging/): Which logger you use depends on where the code runs. Structured templates are mandatory everywhere.

## CI/CD

- [Build Pipeline](https://anvil.st0o0.net/ci/build/): The build has one job: prove the solution compiles cleanly, is formatted, and passes its tests. All commands run from the repository root.
- [GitHub Actions](https://anvil.st0o0.net/ci/github-actions/): Workflows are split by cost: fast checks on every change, slow checks on a schedule. All CI workflows call reusable workflows from [github-workflows](https://github.com/st0o0/github-workflows) - pin t
